chunks: And in the narration of Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
"If he has a residence in Makkah and wishes to fast the seven, he should leave the fasting for the measure of the time of his travel to his family, or for a month, then he fasts."
ai.seo_question: When should a mutamattiʿ residing in Makkah fast the seven days if he cannot afford a sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the timing of the seven days of fasting for the mutamattiʿ who cannot offer a sacrificial animal. If he has a residence in Makkah, he delays fasting for the amount of time it would normally take him to return to his family, or for one month, and then fasts.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3099 - In a narration from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdullah (as):

"If a person resides in Mecca and wishes to fast the seven days, he should delay the fast for a period equivalent to the time it would take to travel to his family or for a month, and then begin fasting."
